clue.text: Scratches, do we hear? It's part of the act

indicators.note: the question asks whether we are hearing it, so the word for scratches is to be taken as spoken

parts.note: a cat claws when it scratches

explanation.surface: A query about scratching noises in the middle of a stage act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'act' looks theatrical but means an Act of Parliament, which is made up of numbered provisions.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute is divided into separate provisions, each one a single section of the legislation.

clue.text: Affected by church atmosphere, have a seat

parts.note: camp means theatrically affected or mannered
the air around us is the atmosphere

explanation.surface: Someone influenced by the mood of a church is invited to sit down.
explanation.definitionFit: A folding stool for outdoor holidays is a kind of portable seat.

clue.text: Stone worker shoring up a barrier

indicators.note: in a down entry the worker sits below and so props up the other pieces from beneath

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across water
the worker is the worker ant of a colony

explanation.surface: A stonemason is propping up a wall or barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoring up' places the worker below A DAM in this down entry, holding it up.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend the hardest of all minerals, unbreakable, was a fabled stone of that name.

clue.text: Lumber a footballer with this swine!

parts.note: to lumber someone with a burden is to saddle them with it
a back is a defensive football player

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry about someone who has burdened a footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swine' reads as an insult, but it is literal: a British breed of pig with a pale band over its shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a breed of pig, black with a white belt round the forequarters.

clue.text: Paper payments to employee

parts.note: a scot is an old tax or payment, as in scot-free
a man can mean a worker, as in master and man

explanation.surface: A newspaper's wage payments to a member of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOT is an old word for a levy or payment, surviving in 'scot-free'. The paper is the Edinburgh daily newspaper of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a long-running Edinburgh daily newspaper.

clue.text: Recesses for drunken directors?

parts.note: someone in their cups is drunk
the directors of a company sit on its boards

explanation.surface: A suggestion that boardrooms are cubbyholes for tipsy executives.
explanation.walkthrough: Directors who are drunk are 'boards in their cups', the idiom for tipsiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage closets are often built into alcoves or wall recesses.

clue.text: Singular garment, a sort of robe

definitions.meaning: a single Roman outer garment, the singular of a Latin plural ending in -ae
a loose draped robe worn by Roman citizens

explanation.definitionFit: The Roman citizen's draped woollen outer garment was a kind of robe.

clue.text: A blemish in mother's make-up

indicators.note: the blemish sits inside the letters for mother and A

parts.note: ma is mother
taken as written
a scar is a blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: A mark spoils mother's cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyelash colouring is one of the cosmetics that make up a face.

clue.text: A way in New York to describe something in woodshed?

indicators.note: the way and A go inside the two letters for New York

parts.note: taken as written
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A New York idiom for whatever lurks in a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to Stella Gibbons' novel Cold Comfort Farm, whose Aunt Ada once saw 'something nasty in the woodshed'.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous phrase from Cold Comfort Farm calls the unspeakable thing in the shed horrid and unpleasant.

clue.text: A queen thus upset a pagan deity .

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, a queen

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means turned upside down, so the word for thus is read backwards

parts.note: so means thus

explanation.surface: A queen is thereby offended by a heathen god.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of love was a heathen divinity.

clue.text: Poor Russian returning to pursue a random course

parts.note: mean can mean poor or shabby

indicators.note: returning means the word for the Russian is read backwards

parts.note: a red is a Soviet Russian

explanation.surface: An impoverished Russian going home and wandering aimlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander is to follow a winding, aimless route, like a river's bends.

clue.text: Secure a South American group of stars

parts.note: to peg something is to secure it
US means American

explanation.surface: Getting hold of a South American band, perhaps celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged horse of myth gives its name to a constellation in the northern sky.

clue.text: Steps possibly stolen by a daily help

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a daily cleaning help

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of stolen may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Dance steps perhaps pinched by the cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges STOLEN into LESTON. A CHAR is a British cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a lively 1920s dance, a set of steps.

clue.text: Course of action about right for the cautious

indicators.note: about means going round, so the course of action surrounds the letter for right

parts.note: a way is a course of action

explanation.surface: A plan that suits careful people.
explanation.definitionFit: Being careful and on guard is a synonym of cautious.

clue.text: . and Lucy upset a drunken oil producer

indicators.note: drunken suggests letters staggering into a new order

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: Lucy is also overturned by an inebriated person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' is the anagram signal; 'upset' looks like one too but here it gives its own letters. The leading dots carry on from the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The gum tree yields an aromatic medicinal oil from its leaves.

clue.text: Port is best in a drunken assembly

indicators.note: a drunken assembly is a disorderly gathering, so the letters are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A claim that port wine is finest at a boozy gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken assembly' rearranges BEST and IN A; 'Port' is a harbour, not wine.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a harbour town on the French Riviera.

clue.text: Tramp around Australia for an evening drink

definitions.meaning: an Australian swagman who turns up at a station at dusk, too late to work but in time for food

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from arriving at dusk: an Outback vagrant, and a cocktail taken at the end of the day.

clue.text: It is said repeatedly when making conversation, of course

definitions.text: It is said repeatedly when making conversation, of course

parts.words: It is said repeatedly when making conversation, of course
parts.note: stage extras mutter one word over and over to sound like talk; the same thing is served as a dessert course

explanation.definitionFit: Actors murmur this word to imitate crowd chatter, and the stalks are stewed for pudding.

clue.text: A hindrance to the principal, this numskull

parts.note: a block is an obstruction
the head is the principal of a school

explanation.surface: An obstacle facing the headteacher is this fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce or dolt is a stupid person.

clue.text: Invaders may cross it to polish up the image

parts.note: to rub something is to polish it up
an icon is an image

explanation.surface: Invading armies cross a frontier while someone shines up a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar crossed this river into Italy, a point of no return.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar's army crossed this Italian river in 49 BC, beginning civil war.

clue.text: MP once a spy?

definitions.meaning: formerly a member of parliament representing a borough
Guy, one of the Cambridge spies who defected to Moscow

explanation.definitionFit: Historically a borough's parliamentary representative bore this title; Guy of that surname spied for the Soviets.

clue.text: Has mop, perhaps — with nothing to clean it

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters of has mop could be in another order

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone has a mop but nothing to wash it with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges HAS MOP into SHAMPO. The mop is really a mop of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To lather and wash a mop of hair is to wash the hair with soap.

clue.text: Lavish payment originally raised for legal enjoyment of property

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word payment
in a down entry raised means the word for is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: use is the legal term for the enjoyment of property

explanation.surface: A generous fee first lifted for a property right.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant and extravagant are synonyms of lavish.

clue.text: First of 5 or last of 24 in Ireland

parts.note: 5 down's answer begins with C
taken as written
24 across ends with K

explanation.surface: A puzzle reference to letters of two other entries, placed in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers point to other answers in this grid.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a city and county in the south of the Irish Republic.

clue.text: Smart shoemaker drops in

indicators.note: the shoemaker drops the word in, losing those letters

parts.note: St Crispin is the patron saint of shoemakers

explanation.surface: A stylish cobbler pays a visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops in' looks like visiting; here 'drops' removes IN from CRISPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp and neat, as in a crisp new uniform, means smart.

clue.text: No easy task for Balaam's supporter

definitions.meaning: the biblical prophet Balaam rode an ass, whose labour this would be

explanation.definitionFit: Drudgery is the sense; the joke is that Balaam's ass carried him, doing the work of a beast of burden.

clue.text: Lear's loyal protector known north of the Border

definitions.meaning: the earl who stays faithful to King Lear in Shakespeare's play
in Scots, ken means know, and this form is its past participle

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's faithful earl shares the name with the Scottish past participle of ken, to know; the Border is England's with Scotland.

clue.text: Lacking energy, proceed with difficulty

definitions.meaning: to walk unevenly because of injury

explanation.definitionFit: Floppy and feeble is one sense; hobbling along on an injured leg is the other.

clue.text: Spaniard involved in capturing a Soviet police chief

indicators.note: capturing means the letters for involved surround the police chief

parts.note: in means involved, as in being in on something
Lavrenti Beria headed Stalin's secret police

explanation.surface: A Spaniard implicated in arresting a Soviet secret-police boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' puts the police chief inside; he ran Stalin's secret police, the NKVD.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal can be a Spaniard.

clue.text: Gun brought back to Britain with Oriental ornament

indicators.note: brought back means the word for the gun is read backwards

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun
UK is the United Kingdom, Britain
E for East, Oriental

explanation.surface: A firearm returned home along with an Eastern trinket.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small carved Japanese toggle, worn as a decorative piece.

clue.text: Circulate wine — it guarantees admission

parts.note: to pass something round is to circulate it
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Pass the port round: it will get you in.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel document allows the holder entry to a foreign country.

clue.text: Go up and throw sand around the church?

indicators.note: around says the jumbled sand goes round the church letters
throw suggests tossing the letters of sand about

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Climb, and fling sand about the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throw' gives ASND, the anagram, which goes 'around' the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb or rise means to go up.
